capability.summary: Run pytest verbosely on one local target and return raw output plus a heuristic summary
capability.description: Executes `[sys.executable, -m, pytest, target_path, -tb, short, -v]` in the inherited working directory. It returns raw streams and heuristically parsed counts. A normal timed `no tests ran` summary usually matches the regex first and, with pytest exit 5, is labeled failed rather than no_tests.
capability.problem_space: Direct pytest execution for a single path with verbose console capture and lightweight summary extraction; not safe test inspection, pytest-json-report output, coverage measurement, test generation, or arbitrary pytest option forwarding.

env_requirements: pytest importable by the current Python interpreter
the target's test dependencies and plugins available in the inherited environment
constraint.io_signature: Input: required target_path string naming an existing file or directory. Executes current Python `-m pytest <target> -tb short -v` with inherited cwd. Output: JSON object with status, pytest exit_code, heuristic summary, raw stdout/stderr, or status=error with message.
accepted_inputs: an existing Python test file, test directory, or other pytest-collectable local path intentionally authorized for execution
constraint.output_shape: Completed subprocess: {status: "passed"|"failed"|"no_tests", exit_code: integer, summary: {text: string, passed: integer, failed: integer, errors: integer, skipped: integer}, stdout: string, stderr: string}, wrapper exit 0 regardless of pytest exit. `no_tests` occurs only when the timing-summary regex finds no match and lowercase stdout still contains `no tests ran`; ordinary timed no-test output usually matches first and becomes status="failed" because pytest exits nonzero. Non-existing target or caught launch/parsing exception: {status: "error", message: string}, wrapper exit 0. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: pytest collection and tests execute arbitrary Python code, plugins, and conftest hooks with inherited permissions/environment and may modify files, spawn processes, or access networks
does not set cwd to the target, forward user pytest options, impose a timeout, truncate output, or terminate hanging tests
summary parsing requires a specific `=== ... in <decimal>s ===` stdout form and uses substring checks, so counts can be missing or inaccurate across pytest versions and outcomes

the no_tests branch is reached only when that regex completely misses and stdout contains `no tests ran`; conventional timed no-test summaries generally match the regex and are reported as failed, not no_tests
the wrapper itself exits 0 for missing targets, test failures, collection errors, and caught exceptions; consumers must inspect JSON status and exit_code

output_contract.description: JSON pytest result with raw streams and heuristic counts; conventional timed no-test runs are generally labeled failed rather than no_tests.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: run pytest on a local test target
capture verbose pytest output and basic result counts
negative_intents: inspect Python tests safely without executing them
produce pytest native JSON or coverage reports
forward arbitrary pytest options or run npm Jest Go or Rust tests
